audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Draft translation of 2 Chronicles 32 aligned to Hebrew witness; preserves Assyrian taunts, YHWH naming, and the Gihon/Millo details. One flagged textual variant at v21 (bracketed form).

verses.restored: After these words and this truth, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah, and encamped against the fortified cities and spoke against them.

familiar.text: After these things, and the establishment thereof, Sennacherib king of Assyria came, and entered into Judah, and encamped against the fenced cities, and thought to win them for himself.

modern.text: After all these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He laid siege to the fortified cities, intending to conquer them for himself.

original.text: אַחֲרֵ֨י הַדְּבָרִ֤ים וְהָאֱמֶת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה בָּ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּבֹ֣א בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וַיִּ֨חַן֙ עַל הֶעָרִ֣ים הַבְּצֻר֔וֹת וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְבִקְעָ֥ם אֵלָֽיו

verses.restored: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come, and that his face was set to wage war against Jerusalem,

familiar.text: And when Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib was come, and that he was purposed to fight against Jerusalem,

modern.text: When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come to make war against Jerusalem,

original.text: וַיַּרְא֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּי בָ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֑יב וּפָנָ֕יו לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עַל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: He took counsel with his princes and his mighty men to stop the springs that were outside the city, and they helped him.

familiar.text: He took counsel with his princes and his mighty men to stop the waters of the fountains which were without the city: and they did help him.

modern.text: he consulted with his leaders and commanders about stopping up the waters of the springs outside the city, and they helped him carry it out.

original.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ עִם שָׂרָיו֙ וְגִבֹּרָ֔יו לִסְתּוֹם֙ אֶת מֵימֵ֣י הָעֲיָנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִח֣וּץ לָעִ֑יר וַֽיַּעְזְרֽוּהוּ

verses.restored: A great people gathered and stopped every spring and the torrent that flowed through the land, saying, Why should the kings of Assyria come and find abundant water?

familiar.text: So there was gathered much people together, who stopped all the fountains, and the brook that ran through the midst of the land, saying, Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?

modern.text: Many people assembled and stopped up all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land. “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?” they said.

original.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ עַם רָ֔ב וַֽיִּסְתְּמוּ֙ אֶת כָּל הַמַּעְיָנ֔וֹת וְאֶת הַנַּ֛חַל הַשּׁוֹטֵ֥ף בְּתוֹךְ הָאָ֖רֶץ לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֤מָּה יָב֨וֹאוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר וּמָצְא֖וּ מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים

verses.restored: He strengthened himself and rebuilt all the broken wall, raised it to the towers, and another wall outside; he repaired the Millo in the city of David, and made many weapons and shields.

familiar.text: Also he strengthened himself, and built up all the wall that was broken, and raised it up to the towers, and another wall without, and repaired Millo in the city of David, and made darts and shields in abundance.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Millo (Hebrew מִלּוֹ) is a fortified terrace or fill in the city of David.

modern.text: Then Hezekiah worked resolutely to rebuild all the broken sections of the wall and to raise up towers on it. He also built an outer wall and reinforced the supporting terraces of the City of David, and he produced an abundance of weapons and shields.

original.text: וַיִּתְחַזַּ֡ק וַיִּבֶן֩ אֶת כָּל הַחוֹמָ֨ה הַפְּרוּצָ֜ה וַיַּ֣עַל עַל הַמִּגְדָּל֗וֹת וְלַח֨וּצָה֙ הַחוֹמָ֣ה אַחֶ֔רֶת וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק אֶת הַמִּלּ֖וֹא עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיַּ֥עַשׂ שֶׁ֛לַח לָרֹ֖ב וּמָגִנִּֽים

verses.restored: He appointed captains of war over the people, gathered them in the public square by the city gate, and spoke to their hearts, saying,

familiar.text: And he set captains of war over the people, and gathered them together to him in the street of the gate of the city, and spake comfortably to them, saying,

modern.text: Hezekiah appointed military commanders over the people and gathered the people in the square of the city gate. Then he encouraged them, saying,

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֛ן שָׂרֵ֥י מִלְחָמ֖וֹת עַל הָעָ֑ם וַיִּקְבְּצֵ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו אֶל רְחוֹב֙ שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֔יר וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר עַל לְבָבָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Be strong and courageous; do not fear or be dismayed before the king of Assyria nor before all the multitude with him; for there are more with us than with him.

familiar.text: Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that is with him: for there be more with us than with him:

modern.text: “Be strong and courageous! Do not be afraid or discouraged before the king of Assyria and the vast army with him, for there is a greater One with us than with him.

original.text: חִזְק֣וּ וְאִמְצ֔וּ אַל תִּֽירְא֣וּ וְאַל תֵּחַ֗תּוּ מִפְּנֵי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וּמִלִּפְנֵ֖י כָּל הֶהָמ֣וֹן אֲשֶׁר עִמּ֑וֹ כִּֽי עִמָּ֥נוּ רַ֖ב מֵעִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is YHWH our God to help us and to fight our battles; and the people rested upon the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

familiar.text: With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is the LORD our God to help us, and to fight our battles. And the people rested themselves upon the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Divine name from Hebrew יְהֹוָה rendered YHWH.

modern.text: With him is only the arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles.” So the people were strengthened by the words of Hezekiah king of Judah. Sennacherib Threatens Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17–37; Isaiah 36:1–22)

original.text: עִמּוֹ֙ זְר֣וֹעַ בָּשָׂ֔ר וְעִמָּ֜נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ לְעָזְרֵ֔נוּ וּלְהִלָּחֵ֖ם מִלְחֲמֹתֵ֑נוּ וַיִּסָּמְכ֣וּ הָעָ֔ם עַל דִּבְרֵ֖י יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem (while he himself was besieging Lachish with all his power), to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah in Jerusalem, saying,

familiar.text: After this did Sennacherib king of Assyria send his servants to Jerusalem, (but he himself laid siege against Lachish, and all his power with him,) unto Hezekiah king of Judah, and unto all Judah that were at Jerusalem, saying,

modern.text: Later, as Sennacherib king of Assyria and all his forces besieged Lachish, he sent his servants to Jerusalem with a message for King Hezekiah of Judah and all the people of Judah who were in Jerusalem:

original.text: אַ֣חַר זֶ֗ה שָׁ֠לַח סַנְחֵרִ֨יב מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֤וּר עֲבָדָיו֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלַ֔יְמָה וְהוּא֙ עַל לָכִ֔ישׁ וְכָל מֶמְשַׁלְתּ֖וֹ עִמּ֑וֹ עַל יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְעַל כָּל יְהוּדָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: On what do you trust, that you sit in a siege in Jerusalem?

familiar.text: Thus saith Sennacherib king of Assyria, Whereon do ye trust, that ye abide in the siege in Jerusalem?

modern.text: “This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: What is the basis of your confidence, that you remain in Jerusalem under siege?

original.text: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֔ר סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר עַל מָה֙ אַתֶּ֣ם בֹּטְחִ֔ים וְיֹשְׁבִ֥ים בְּמָצ֖וֹר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Does not Hezekiah persuade you to surrender yourselves to die of famine and thirst, saying, YHWH our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria?

familiar.text: Doth not Hezekiah persuade you to give over yourselves to die by famine and by thirst, saying, The LORD our God shall deliver us out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

modern.text: Is not Hezekiah misleading you to give you over to death by famine and thirst when he says, ‘The LORD our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria?’

original.text: הֲלֹ֤א יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ מַסִּ֣ית אֶתְכֶ֔ם לָתֵ֣ת אֶתְכֶ֔ם לָמ֛וּת בְּרָעָ֥ב וּבְצָמָ֖א לֵאמֹ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ יַצִּילֵ֕נוּ מִכַּ֖ף מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר

verses.restored: Has not this Hezekiah removed his high places and his altars and said to Judah and Jerusalem, 'Before one altar you shall bow down and burn incense'?

familiar.text: Hath not the same Hezekiah taken away his high places and his altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying, Ye shall worship before one altar, and burn incense upon it?

modern.text: Did not Hezekiah himself remove His high places and His altars and say to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship before one altar, and on it you shall burn sacrifices’?

original.text: הֲלֹא הוּא֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ הֵסִ֥יר אֶת בָּמֹתָ֖יו וְאֶת מִזְבְּחֹתָ֑יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָ֤ה וְלִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לִפְנֵ֨י מִזְבֵּ֧חַ אֶחָ֛ד תִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ וְעָלָ֥יו תַּקְטִֽירוּ

verses.restored: Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Could the gods of those peoples deliver their lands from my hand?

familiar.text: Know ye not what I and my fathers have done unto all the people of other lands? were the gods of the nations of those lands any ways able to deliver their lands out of mine hand?

modern.text: Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Have the gods of these nations ever been able to deliver their land from my hand?

original.text: הֲלֹ֣א תֵדְע֗וּ מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י וַאֲבוֹתַ֔י לְכֹ֖ל עַמֵּ֣י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת הֲיָכ֣וֹל יָֽכְל֗וּ אֱלֹהֵי֙ גּוֹיֵ֣ הָאֲרָצ֔וֹת לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי

verses.restored: Which of all the gods of those nations whom my fathers destroyed could save his people from my hand? How then would your God be able to save you from my hand?

familiar.text: Who was there among all the gods of those nations that my fathers utterly destroyed, that could deliver his people out of mine hand, that your God should be able to deliver you out of mine hand?

modern.text: Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers devoted to destruction has been able to deliver his people from my hand? How then can your God deliver you from my hand?

original.text: מִ֠י בְּֽכָל אֱלֹהֵ֞י הַגּוֹיִ֤ם הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱרִ֣ימוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָכ֔וֹל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת עַמּ֖וֹ מִיָּדִ֑י כִּ֤י יוּכַל֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי

verses.restored: Now therefore let not Hezekiah deceive you or make you trust in this manner; do not believe him; for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers—how much less will your God deliver you?

familiar.text: Now therefore let not Hezekiah deceive you, nor persuade you on this manner, neither yet believe him: for no god of any nation or kingdom was able to deliver his people out of mine hand, and out of the hand of my fathers: how much less shall your God deliver you out of mine hand?

modern.text: So now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you, and do not let him mislead you like this. Do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God deliver you from my hand!”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה אַל יַשִּׁיא֩ אֶתְכֶ֨ם חִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וְאַל יַסִּ֨ית אֶתְכֶ֣ם כָּזֹאת֮ וְאַל תַּאֲמִ֣ינוּ לוֹ֒ כִּי לֹ֣א יוּכַ֗ל כָּל אֱל֨וֹהַ֙ כָּל גּ֣וֹי וּמַמְלָכָ֔ה לְהַצִּ֥יל עַמּ֛וֹ מִיָּדִ֖י וּמִיַּ֣ד אֲבוֹתָ֑י אַ֚ף כִּ֣י אֱֽלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם לֹא יַצִּ֥ילוּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדִֽי

verses.restored: Moreover, his servants spoke against YHWH the God and against His servant Hezekiah.

familiar.text: And his servants spake yet more against the LORD God, and against his servant Hezekiah.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew frames these as public speeches against deity and king.

modern.text: And the servants of Sennacherib spoke further against the LORD God and against His servant Hezekiah.

original.text: וְעוֹד֙ דִּבְּר֣וּ עֲבָדָ֔יו עַל יְהוָ֖ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ עַבְדּֽוֹ

verses.restored: He also wrote letters to revile YHWH God of Israel and to speak against Him, saying that as the gods of the nations have not delivered their peoples from my hand, so YHWH will not deliver His people from my hand.

familiar.text: He wrote also letters to rail on the LORD God of Israel, and to speak against him, saying, As the gods of the nations of other lands have not delivered their people out of mine hand, so shall not the God of Hezekiah deliver his people out of mine hand.

modern.text: He also wrote letters mocking the LORD, the God of Israel, and saying against Him: “Just as the gods of the nations did not deliver their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver His people from my hand.”

original.text: וּסְפָרִ֣ים כָּתַ֔ב לְחָרֵ֕ף לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֵֽאמֹ֨ר עָלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֵּֽאלֹהֵ֞י גּוֹיֵ֤ הָאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא הִצִּ֤ילוּ עַמָּם֙ מִיָּדִ֔י כֵּ֣ן לֹֽא יַצִּ֞יל אֱלֹהֵ֧י יְחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עַמּ֖וֹ מִיָּדִֽי

verses.restored: Then they cried with a loud voice in the Jewish tongue to the people on the wall in Jerusalem, to frighten and terrify them that they might take the city.

familiar.text: Then they cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ speech unto the people of Jerusalem that were on the wall, to affright them, and to trouble them; that they might take the city.

modern.text: Then the Assyrians called out loudly in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten and terrify them in order to capture the city.

original.text: וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ בְקוֹל גָּד֜וֹל יְהוּדִ֗ית עַל עַ֤ם יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַֽחוֹמָ֔ה לְיָֽרְאָ֖ם וּֽלְבַהֲלָ֑ם לְמַ֖עַן יִלְכְּד֥וּ אֶת הָעִֽיר

verses.restored: They spoke against the God of Jerusalem as against the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.

familiar.text: And they spake against the God of Jerusalem, as against the gods of the people of the earth, which were the work of the hands of man.

modern.text: They spoke against the God of Jerusalem as they had spoken against the gods of the peoples of the earth—the work of human hands. Jerusalem Delivered from the Assyrians (2 Kings 19:35–37; Isaiah 37:36–38)

original.text: וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל אֱלֹהֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כְּעַ֗ל אֱלֹהֵי֙ עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם

verses.restored: For this cause Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz, prayed and cried to heaven.

familiar.text: And for this cause Hezekiah the king, and the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz, prayed and cried to heaven.

modern.text: In response, King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz cried out to heaven in prayer,

original.text: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֞ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וִֽישַֽׁעְיָ֧הוּ בֶן אָמ֛וֹץ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל זֹ֑את וַֽיִּזְעֲק֖וּ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

verses.restored: Then YHWH sent an angel, who cut off every mighty man of valor, commanders and officers in the camp of the king of Assyria; and he returned with shame to his own land. And when he came into the house of his god, those who came forth of his own body slew him there with the sword.

familiar.text: And the LORD sent an angel, which cut off all the mighty men of valour, and the leaders and captains in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land. And when he was come into the house of his god, they that came forth of his own bowels slew him there with the sword.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew text has a bracketed reading (ומיציאו / וּמִיצִיאֵי); variant affects phrase about those coming out of his bowels—witness check recommended.

modern.text: and the LORD sent an angel who annihilated every mighty man of valor and every leader and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he withdrew to his own land in disgrace. And when he entered the temple of his god, some of his own sons struck him down with the sword.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ מַלְאָ֔ךְ וַיַּכְחֵ֞ד כָּל גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֨יִל֙ וְנָגִ֣יד וְשָׂ֔ר בְּמַחֲנֵ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּשָׁב֩ בְּבֹ֨שֶׁת פָּנִ֜ים לְאַרְצ֗וֹ וַיָּבֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהָ֔יו ומיציאו מֵעָ֔יו שָׁ֖ם הִפִּילֻ֥הוּ בֶחָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Thus YHWH saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all others, and guided them on every side.

familiar.text: Thus the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib the king of Assyria, and from the hand of all other, and guided them on every side.

modern.text: So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the hands of King Sennacherib of Assyria and all the others, and He gave them rest on every side.

original.text: וַיּוֹשַׁע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וְאֵ֣ת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם מִיַּ֛ד סַנְחֵרִ֥יב מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר וּמִיַּד כֹּ֑ל וַֽיְנַהֲלֵ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב

verses.restored: And many brought gifts to YHWH to Jerusalem and presents to Hezekiah king of Judah; so he was exalted in the sight of all the nations thereafter.

familiar.text: And many brought gifts unto the LORD to Jerusalem, and presents to Hezekiah king of Judah: so that he was magnified in the sight of all nations from thenceforth.

modern.text: Many brought offerings to Jerusalem for the LORD and valuable gifts for Hezekiah king of Judah, and from then on he was exalted in the eyes of all nations. Hezekiah’s Illness and Recovery (2 Kings 20:1–11; Isaiah 38:1–8)

original.text: וְ֠רַבִּים מְבִיאִ֨ים מִנְחָ֤ה לַיהוָה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּמִ֨גְדָּנ֔וֹת לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּנַּשֵּׂ֛א לְעֵינֵ֥י כָל הַגּוֹיִ֖ם מֵאַֽחֲרֵי כֵֽן

verses.restored: In those days Hezekiah was sick to death; he prayed to YHWH, and YHWH spoke to him and gave him a sign.

familiar.text: In those days Hezekiah was sick to the death, and prayed unto the LORD: and he spake unto him, and he gave him a sign.

modern.text: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. So he prayed to the LORD, who spoke to him and gave him a sign.

original.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ עַד לָמ֑וּת וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ אֶל יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ וּמוֹפֵ֖ת נָ֥תַן לֽוֹ

verses.restored: But Hezekiah did not repay according to the benefit shown him; for his heart was proud, therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.

familiar.text: But Hezekiah rendered not again according to the benefit done unto him; for his heart was lifted up: therefore there was wrath upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.

modern.text: But because his heart was proud, Hezekiah did not repay the favor shown to him. Therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.

original.text: וְלֹא כִגְמֻ֤ל עָלָיו֙ הֵשִׁ֣יב יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּ֥י גָבַ֖הּ לִבּ֑וֹ וַיְהִ֤י עָלָיו֙ קֶ֔צֶף וְעַל יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: But Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the wrath of YHWH did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the LORD came not upon them in the days of Hezekiah.

modern.text: Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart—he and the people of Jerusalem—so that the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them during the days of Hezekiah.

original.text: וַיִּכָּנַ֤ע יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ בְּגֹ֣בַהּ לִבּ֔וֹ ה֖וּא וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא בָ֤א עֲלֵיהֶם֙ קֶ֣צֶף יְהוָ֔ה בִּימֵ֖י יְחִזְקִיָּֽהוּ

verses.restored: And Hezekiah had great riches and honor; he made for himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all manner of desirable vessels,

familiar.text: And Hezekiah had exceeding much riches and honour: and he made himself treasuries for silver, and for gold, and for precious stones, and for spices, and for shields, and for all manner of pleasant jewels;

modern.text: Hezekiah had very great riches and honor, and he made treasuries for his silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuable articles.

original.text: וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וְאֹֽצָר֣וֹת עָֽשָׂה ל֠וֹ לְכֶ֨סֶף וּלְזָהָ֜ב וּלְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֗ה וְלִבְשָׂמִים֙ וּלְמָ֣גִנִּ֔ים וּלְכֹ֖ל כְּלֵ֥י חֶמְדָּֽה

verses.restored: Storehouses also for grain, wine, and oil; stalls for all kinds of beasts and folds for flocks.

familiar.text: Storehouses also for the increase of corn, and wine, and oil; and stalls for all manner of beasts, and cotes for flocks.

modern.text: He also made storehouses for the harvest of grain and new wine and oil, stalls for all kinds of livestock, and pens for the flocks.

original.text: וּמִ֨סְכְּנ֔וֹת לִתְבוּאַ֥ת דָּגָ֖ן וְתִיר֣וֹשׁ וְיִצְהָ֑ר וְאֻֽרָוֺת֙ לְכָל בְּהֵמָ֣ה וּבְהֵמָ֔ה וַעֲדָרִ֖ים לָאֲוֵרֽוֹת

verses.restored: He acquired cities for himself and very much livestock, sheep and cattle; for God had given him exceedingly much wealth.

familiar.text: Moreover he provided him cities, and possessions of flocks and herds in abundance: for God had given him substance very much.

modern.text: He made cities for himself, and he acquired herds of sheep and cattle in abundance, for God gave him very great wealth.

original.text: וְעָרִים֙ עָ֣שָׂה ל֔וֹ וּמִקְנֵה צֹ֥אן וּבָקָ֖ר לָרֹ֑ב כִּ֤י נָֽתַן לוֹ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים רְכ֖וּשׁ רַ֥ב מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: This Hezekiah stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and led them straight down to the west side of the city of David; and Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

familiar.text: This same Hezekiah also stopped the upper watercourse of Gihon, and brought it straight down to the west side of the city of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Gihon (Hebrew גיחון) is the spring of Jerusalem; engineering project noted here.

modern.text: It was Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the Spring of Gihon and channeled it down to the west side of the City of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all that he did.

original.text: וְה֣וּא יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ סָתַם֙ אֶת מוֹצָ֞א מֵימֵ֤י גִיחוֹן֙ הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן וַֽיַּישְּׁרֵ֥ם לְמַֽטָּה מַּעְרָ֖בָה לְעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיַּצְלַ֥ח יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכָֽל מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ

verses.restored: As for the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon who sent to inquire about the wonder that was done in the land, God left him to try him, to know all that was in his heart.

familiar.text: Howbeit in the business of the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who sent unto him to enquire of the wonder that was done in the land, God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew indicates 'God left him' (testing) — theological nuance requires witness comparison.

modern.text: And so when ambassadors of the rulers of Babylon were sent to him to inquire about the wonder that had happened in the land, God left him alone to test him, that He might know all that was in Hezekiah’s heart. Hezekiah’s Death

original.text: וְכֵ֞ן בִּמְלִיצֵ֣י שָׂרֵ֣י בָּבֶ֗ל הַֽמְשַׁלְּחִ֤ים עָלָיו֙ לִדְרֹ֗שׁ הַמּוֹפֵת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה בָאָ֔רֶץ עֲזָב֖וֹ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים לְנַ֨סּוֹת֔וֹ לָדַ֖עַת כָּל בִּלְבָבֽוֹ

verses.restored: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his kindnesses—behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz and in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his goodness, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, and in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his deeds of loving devotion, they are indeed written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

original.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ וַחֲסָדָ֑יו הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים בַּחֲז֞וֹן יְשַֽׁעְיָ֤הוּ בֶן אָמוֹץ֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא עַל סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵי יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Hezekiah slept with his fathers; they buried him on the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David. And all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem honored him at his death; and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the chiefest of the sepulchres of the sons of David: and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did him honour at his death. And Manasseh his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Hezekiah rested with his fathers and was buried in the upper tombs of David’s descendants. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem paid him honor at his death. And his son Manasseh reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻהוּ֮ בְּֽמַעֲלֵה֮ קִבְרֵ֣י בְנֵי דָוִיד֒ וְכָבוֹד֙ עָֽשׂוּ ל֣וֹ בְמוֹת֔וֹ כָּל יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו
